text:
maria: Heads-up — profiler traces from the canary run of the tokenflow-splitter heuristic. Seeing a latency regression on 8k sequences when the splitter hands off from prefill -> decode. decode tail spiked ~2.3x compared to baseline. attaching quick sampling flame and short logs.

maria: p95 numbers: baseline decode p95=85ms, canary decode p95=195ms. prefill p50 unchanged. KV hit rate dropped after handoff. :eyes:

maria: command we used to collect traces:```bash
perf-collect --target tokenflow-splitter --dur 300 --svg out.svg
# sample log excerpt
[2026-03-17T10:01:12Z] HANDOFF prefill->decode req_id=abcd1234 queue_latency=4ms
[2026-03-17T10:01:12Z] DECODE_START req_id=abcd1234 kernel=matmul-tiled-accel stream=3
[2026-03-17T10:01:12Z] DECODE_END req_id=abcd1234 latency=210ms
```

dan: :thinking_face: did we flip the matmul kernel selector yesterday? saw a kernel bump in the deploy notes.

maria: yes — kernel selector bumped to prefer tiled-accel (v1.4.3). baseline used generic-matmul-compat. regression correlates with that change + split handoff pattern.

sasha: Could be KV cache thrashing on handoff. Are we draining or re-allocating KV on split?

maria: KV metrics: overall hit-rate for sessions with handoff went from ~61% -> 47% after the bump. hot-key eviction rate up 3x during the window after handoff. Token budget also plays a role — splitter currently assigns decode token_budget=8 by policy for these requests.

patrick: Two quick levers: increase decode token_budget to 12 for long sequences, or prefer colocated lanes for prefill+decode so we avoid cold KV on handoff. Both are low-risk flags.

kevin: We also enabled micro-slicing fair-queue yesterday (quantum=4 tokens). I wonder if the quantum is too small and we get extra GPU stream context switches — logs show repeated stream rebinds around handoff.

deploy-bot: canary-deploy: tokenflow-splitter v2 rolled to canary cluster canary-a at 2026-03-17T10:12Z.

maria: quick repro (run on perf box):```bash
# reproduce with loadgen
./loadgen --model redwood-small --seq-len 8192 --splitter tokenflow-splitter --qps 60 --dur 600
# observe p95 using rtt-agg
./tools/rtt-agg --in loadgen.out --p95
```

julia: ran local repro in perf lab. Flipping kernel selector back to generic-matmul-compat reduces decode p95 by ~30%, but prefill p50 increases ~8%. So it's a trade.

dan: For interactive apps we prioritize tail. Might be acceptable to prefer the fallback kernel for now.

sasha: Proposal: introduce phase-aware scheduler tweak + KV warmup on handoff. Specifically: (1) keep decode batches contiguous for at least N decode steps to avoid interleaving, (2) extend KV warmup window by +2 tokens during decode handoff so hot KV gets warmed before decode heavy ops, (3) bump decode token_budget to 12 for long seq class, and (4) increase prefill batch-formation timeout from 5ms -> 10ms to allow larger prefill aggregation.

kevin: +1. Also add a metric: "handoff_same_stream_ratio" to detect how often prefill->decode share the same GPU stream. If that falls, warn.

maria: I'll open a small PR with an opt-in flag for the phase-aware changes and a perf harness that runs the repro. Plan: fly flag in canary for 12h, run loadgen, collect p95/p99, KV hit/ejection, and kernel occupancy. If good, roll to staging and then prod.

patrick: ping me before canary roll. happy to own rollout notes and rollback criteria. :thumbsup:

maria: thanks — creating the PR and will add the raw traces to the issue.

kevin: side note — we should also add a short-term mitigation: auto-fallback of kernel selector when handoff followed by decode latency spike >2x for a minute. Low-risk and self-healing.

julia: agreed. I'll sketch the fallback patch after the PR lands.

maria: tagging follow-ups: @dan (decision on kernel), @patrick (rollout), @sasha (scheduler patch), @julia (fallback).
